   231	/-- The Fourier form of an expanded point effect as a normalized character
   232	sum of the expanded observables.  This is the first display of
   233	`def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   234	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   235	theorem expPointOp_eq_inv_card_smul_sum (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   236	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   237	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
   238	    S.expPointOp side W u a =
   239	      (Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   240	        ∑ r, phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)) • S.expObs side W r u := by
   241	  unfold expPointOp
   242	  rw [averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_eq_inv_card_smul_sum]
   243	
   244	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the product of two normalized weighted sums
   245	is the normalized double sum of the weighted products, indexed by pairs. -/
   246	theorem smul_sum_mul_smul_sum {ι K : Type*} [Fintype K] [Fintype ι]
   247	    (c : ℂ) (α β : K → ℂ) (X Z : K → Op ι) :
   248	    (c • ∑ r, α r • X r) * (c • ∑ s, β s • Z s) =
   249	      (c * c) • ∑ rs : K × K, (α rs.1 * β rs.2) • (X rs.1 * Z rs.2) := by
   250	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, smul_mul_smul_comm, Finset.sum_mul_sum]
   251	  congr 1
   252	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun s _ => ?_
   253	  rw [smul_mul_smul_comm]
   254	
   255	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the product of two normalized weighted sums
   256	in the opposite order, indexed by the same pairs. -/
   257	theorem smul_sum_mul_smul_sum_swap {ι K : Type*} [Fintype K] [Fintype ι]
   258	    (c : ℂ) (α β : K → ℂ) (X Z : K → Op ι) :
   259	    (c • ∑ s, β s • Z s) * (c • ∑ r, α r • X r) =
   260	      (c * c) • ∑ rs : K × K, (α rs.1 * β rs.2) • (Z rs.2 * X rs.1) := by
   261	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right, smul_mul_smul_comm, Finset.sum_mul_sum]
   262	  congr 1
   263	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun s _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => ?_
   264	  rw [smul_mul_smul_comm, mul_comm (β s)]

   266	/-- The commutator of two field-valued point effects is the Fourier transform
   267	of the commutators of the expanded observables. -/
   268	theorem expPointOp_commutator_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   269	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a b : PauliScalar P) :
   270	    S.expPointOp side .X x a * S.expPointOp side .Z z b -
   271	        S.expPointOp side .Z z b * S.expPointOp side .X x a =
   272	      ((Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
   273	          (Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   274	        ∑ rs : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   275	          (phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (a * rs.1)) *
   276	              phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (b * rs.2))) •
   277	            (S.expObs side .X rs.1 x * S.expObs side .Z rs.2 z -
   278	              S.expObs side .Z rs.2 z * S.expObs side .X rs.1 x) := by
   279	  rw [expPointOp_eq_inv_card_smul_sum, expPointOp_eq_inv_card_smul_sum,
   280	    smul_sum_mul_smul_sum, smul_sum_mul_smul_sum_swap, ← smul_sub,
   281	    ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   282	  congr 1
   283	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun rs _ => ?_
   284	  rw [smul_sub]

   286	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: an operator applied to a state is linear in
   287	the operator over finite sums. -/
   288	theorem applyOperatorToState_finsetSum {ι γ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   289	    (s : Finset γ) (M : γ → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   290	    applyOperatorToState (∑ x ∈ s, M x) ψ =
   291	      ∑ x ∈ s, applyOperatorToState (M x) ψ := by
   292	  unfold applyOperatorToState
   293	  simp only [map_sum, LinearMap.sum_apply]
   294	
   295	/-- Parseval transfer, pointwise in the point pair: the summed squared norms of
   296	the placed commutators of the field-valued point effects equal the average over
   297	`(r, s)` of the squared norms of the placed commutators of the expanded
   298	observables. -/
   299	theorem sum_norm_place_expPointOp_commutator_sq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   300	    (p : Placement) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   301	    ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   302	        ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p
   303	          (S.expPointOp p.side .X x ab.1 * S.expPointOp p.side .Z z ab.2 -
   304	            S.expPointOp p.side .Z z ab.2 * S.expPointOp p.side .X x ab.1))
   305	          S.psiHat‖ ^ 2 =
   306	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P))
   307	        (fun rs => ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p
   308	          (S.expObs p.side .X rs.1 x * S.expObs p.side .Z rs.2 z -
   309	            S.expObs p.side .Z rs.2 z * S.expObs p.side .X rs.1 x))
   310	          S.psiHat‖ ^ 2) := by
   311	  set v : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P →
   312	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   313	    fun rs => applyOperatorToState (S.place p
   314	      (S.expObs p.side .X rs.1 x * S.expObs p.side .Z rs.2 z -
   315	        S.expObs p.side .Z rs.2 z * S.expObs p.side .X rs.1 x)) S.psiHat
   316	  set c : ℂ := (Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℂ)⁻¹
   317	  have hpt : ∀ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   318	      applyOperatorToState (S.place p
   319	          (S.expPointOp p.side .X x ab.1 * S.expPointOp p.side .Z z ab.2 -
   320	            S.expPointOp p.side .Z z ab.2 * S.expPointOp p.side .X x ab.1))
   321	          S.psiHat =
   322	        (c * c) • ∑ rs : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   323	          (phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (ab.1 * rs.1)) *
   324	              phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (ab.2 * rs.2))) • v rs := by
   325	    intro ab
   326	    rw [expPointOp_commutator_eq, place_smul, place_finsetSum,
   327	      WinImplications.applyOperatorToState_smul_op, applyOperatorToState_finsetSum]
   328	    congr 1
   329	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun rs _ => ?_
   330	    rw [place_smul, WinImplications.applyOperatorToState_smul_op]
   331	  have hparseval := sum_norm_sum_smul_sq_of_orthogonal
   332	    (fun (ab rs : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
   333	      phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (ab.1 * rs.1)) *
   334	        phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (ab.2 * rs.2)))
   335	    ((Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℝ) ^ 2)
   336	    (fun rs rs' => sum_pairCharacter_mul_pairCharacter rs rs') v
   337	  have hq : (0 : ℝ) < (Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℝ) := by
   338	    exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_pos
   339	  have hcnorm : ‖c * c‖ = ((Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℝ) ^ 2)⁻¹ := by
   340	    simp only [c, norm_mul, norm_inv, Complex.norm_natCast]
   341	    rw [sq, mul_inv]
   342	  calc ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   343	        ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p
   344	          (S.expPointOp p.side .X x ab.1 * S.expPointOp p.side .Z z ab.2 -
   345	            S.expPointOp p.side .Z z ab.2 * S.expPointOp p.side .X x ab.1))
   346	          S.psiHat‖ ^ 2
   347	      = ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   348	          ‖c * c‖ ^ 2 * ‖∑ rs : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   349	            (phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (ab.1 * rs.1)) *
   350	              phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (ab.2 * rs.2))) • v rs‖ ^ 2 := by
   351	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ab _ => ?_
   352	        rw [hpt, norm_smul, mul_pow]
   353	    _ = ‖c * c‖ ^ 2 * (((Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) : ℝ) ^ 2) *
   354	          ∑ rs, ‖v rs‖ ^ 2) := by
   355	        rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hparseval]
   356	    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P))
   357	          (fun rs => ‖v rs‖ ^ 2) := by
   358	        rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, Fintype.card_prod, hcnorm]
   359	        push_cast
   360	        field_simp
   361	
   362	/-- The field-valued expanded point measurements approximately commute on each
   363	of the four register placements, with the error of item 2 of
   364	`lem:qld-comm-cons`.  The estimate is transferred from the binary refinements
   365	of the source by the Parseval identity, without loss in the field size.  Paper
   366	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:466-505`,
   367	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:1139-1210`; the
   368	role of this form in the proof of `lem:qld-4-10` is explained in
   369	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`. -/
   370	theorem expPoint_comm :
   371	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
   372	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   373	        (p : Placement),
   374	        opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   375	          (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p
   376	            ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   377	              (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   378	          (fun xz ab => S.place p
   379	            ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   380	              (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   381	          S.psiHat ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε := by
   382	  obtain ⟨C, hC, h⟩ := exists_twistedCommutator_avg_le
   383	  refine ⟨C, hC, ?_⟩
   384	  intro P ε S p
   385	  have hε : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ε := by
   386	    have hv := WinImplications.strategy_value_le_one S.toStrategy
   387	    have hw := S.win
   388	    linarith
   389	  have hnorm : ∀ (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   390	      (rs : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P),
   391	      ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p
   392	          (S.expObs p.side .X rs.1 x * S.expObs p.side .Z rs.2 z -
   393	            S.expObs p.side .Z rs.2 z * S.expObs p.side .X rs.1 x))
   394	          S.psiHat‖ ^ 2 =
   395	        ‖applyOperatorToState
   396	          (S.placeStrategySide p.side (S.twistedCommutator p.side (x, z, rs.1, rs.2)))
   397	          S.toStrategy.ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   398	    intro x z rs
   399	    rw [expObs_commutator S p.side (x, z, rs.1, rs.2),
   400	      norm_place_heteroKron_psiHat S p _ _ (tauX_mul_tauZ_isometry P (x, z, rs.1, rs.2))]
   401	  have hfamily : opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   402	      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p
   403	        ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   404	          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   405	      (fun xz ab => S.place p
   406	        ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   407	          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   408	      S.psiHat =
   409	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliTuple P)) (fun ω =>
   410	        ‖applyOperatorToState
   411	          (S.placeStrategySide p.side (S.twistedCommutator p.side ω))
   412	          S.toStrategy.ψ‖ ^ 2) := by
   413	    unfold opFamilyDistSq
   414	    calc avgOver (uniformDistribution (PointPair P)) (fun xz =>
   415	          ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   416	            ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place p
   417	                ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   418	                  (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) -
   419	              S.place p ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   420	                (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2)
   421	        = avgOver (uniformDistribution (PointPair P)) (fun xz =>
   422	            avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P))
   423	              (fun rs => ‖applyOperatorToState
   424	                (S.placeStrategySide p.side
   425	                  (S.twistedCommutator p.side (xz.1, xz.2, rs.1, rs.2)))
   426	                S.toStrategy.ψ‖ ^ 2)) := by
   427	          refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun xz => ?_
   428	          rw [← avgOver_congr _ _ _ (hnorm xz.1 xz.2),
   429	            ← sum_norm_place_expPointOp_commutator_sq S p xz.1 xz.2]
   430	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun ab _ => ?_
   431	          rw [place_sub]
   432	          rfl
   433	      _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (PointPair P × (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P)))
   434	            (fun q => ‖applyOperatorToState
   435	              (S.placeStrategySide p.side
   436	                (S.twistedCommutator p.side (q.1.1, q.1.2, q.2.1, q.2.2)))
   437	              S.toStrategy.ψ‖ ^ 2) :=
   438	          (avgOver_uniform_prod (fun (xz : PointPair P)
   439	            (rs : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => ‖applyOperatorToState
   440	              (S.placeStrategySide p.side
   441	                (S.twistedCommutator p.side (xz.1, xz.2, rs.1, rs.2)))
   442	              S.toStrategy.ψ‖ ^ 2)).symm
   443	      _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (PauliTuple P)) (fun ω =>
   444	            ‖applyOperatorToState
   445	              (S.placeStrategySide p.side (S.twistedCommutator p.side ω))
   446	              S.toStrategy.ψ‖ ^ 2) := by
   447	          rw [avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodAssoc (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   448	            (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P))]
   449	          rfl
   450	  rw [hfamily]
   451	  exact h P ε S p.side hε
   452

     3	/-!
     4	# Expanded line measurements
     5	
     6	This module constructs the expanded line measurements by convolving a strategy
     7	line measurement with the Pauli-register line projectors, and records that the
     8	result is a projective measurement whose effects vanish, on an axis-parallel
     9	line, outside the embedded degree-`d` outcome space. It also introduces the
    10	fine strategy--Pauli product measurement of which the expanded line
    11	measurement is the addition postprocessing, and the evaluation-class and
    12	point-effect families used by the consistency estimates.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The declarations formalize `def:expanded-line-measurement`, whose paper
    17	source is
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The tensor placement of a sum of operators is the sum of the tensor
    31	placements, in both factors. Formalization-only auxiliary for the convolution
    32	of `def:expanded-line-measurement`. The same identity is proved as
    33	`heteroKron_sum_sum` in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/ExpandedDefs.lean`, where
    34	it is `private` and therefore invisible from this file; consolidating the two
    35	copies into the module that defines `heteroKron` is tracked by issue #204. -/
    36	private theorem heteroKron_sum_sum {α β ι κ : Type*}
    37	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] (A : α → Op ι) (B : β → Op κ) :
    38	    heteroKron (∑ x, A x) (∑ y, B y) =
    39	      ∑ x, ∑ y, heteroKron (A x) (B y) := by
    40	  ext ⟨i, k⟩ ⟨j, l⟩
    41	  unfold heteroKron Matrix.kronecker Matrix.kroneckerMap
    42	  simp only [Matrix.of_apply, Matrix.sum_apply]
    43	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    44	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    45	  intro x hx
    46	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    47	
    48	/-- The tensor placement of a zero left factor vanishes. This zero law and its
    49	companion below are the two remaining linearity facts about `heteroKron` used
    50	by the expanded line measurements; they are stated here, in the first module
    51	that needs them, because the tensor-placement lemmas of
    52	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/Defs.lean` do not yet record them. Moving them there,
    53	next to `heteroKron_mul` and `heteroKron_one_one`, is tracked by issue #204. -/
    54	theorem heteroKron_zero_left {ι κ : Type*} (B : Op κ) :
    55	    heteroKron (0 : Op ι) B = 0 := by
    56	  unfold heteroKron
    57	  exact Matrix.zero_kronecker B
    58	
    59	/-- The tensor placement of a zero right factor vanishes. -/
    60	theorem heteroKron_zero_right {ι κ : Type*} (A : Op ι) :
    61	    heteroKron A (0 : Op κ) = 0 := by
    62	  unfold heteroKron
    63	  exact Matrix.kronecker_zero A

    69	/-- The line measurement of a projective strategy is again projective: folding
    70	the answers of a line question into a coefficient list is a postprocessing, and
    71	postprocessing preserves projectivity. This is the line analogue of the point
    72	measurement projectivity; both follow because postprocessing preserves
    73	projectivity. The line form is what the projectivity assertion of
    74	`def:expanded-line-measurement` needs, paper
    75	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. Stating the two uniformly
    76	in one place is tracked by issue #204. -/
    77	theorem lineMeas_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    78	    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
    79	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.lineMeas side W line) := by
    80	  apply SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective
    81	  cases side with
    82	  | alice => exact S.isProjective.1 _
    83	  | bob => exact S.isProjective.2 _
    84	
    85	/-- On an axis-parallel line, strategy line effects vanish outside the
    86	embedded degree-`d` subspace: every prescribed answer is a degree-`d`
    87	coefficient list padded by zero. This is the strategy half of the last
    88	assertion of `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
    89	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
    90	theorem lineMeas_effect_eq_zero_of_axis (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    91	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
    92	    (haxis : line.kind = .axis) (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
    93	    (hf : ¬ f.FitsDegree P.d) :
    94	    (S.lineMeas side W line).effect f = 0 := by
    95	  cases line with
    96	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero =>
    97	      simp [LineDesc.kind] at haxis
    98	  | axis base seed baseFixed =>
    99	      unfold lineMeas
   100	      rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   101	      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   102	      intro a ha
   103	      exfalso
   104	      apply hf
   105	      rw [← (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2]
   106	      intro i hi
   107	      have hi' : ¬ i.val < P.d + 1 := by omega
   108	      cases a <;> simp [lineAnswerOrZero, DegPoly.padTo, hi']
   109	
   110	/-- The convolution of a strategy line effect with the corresponding
   111	Pauli-register line projector. This is the displayed definition of
   112	`hat M^(Line,W),line_f`, paper
   113	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`, blueprint
   114	`def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
   115	noncomputable def expLineOp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   116	    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   117	    (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   118	  ∑ pair ∈ Finset.univ.filter
   119	      (fun pair : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   120	          DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) => pair.1 + pair.2 = f),
   121	    heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect pair.1)
   122	      (tauLineProj P W line pair.2)
   123	
   124	/-- Expanded line effects are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity
   125	obligation of `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
   126	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
   127	theorem expLineOp_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   128	    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   129	    (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
   130	    0 ≤ S.expLineOp side W line f := by
   131	  unfold expLineOp
   132	  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun pair _ => Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
   133	    ((S.lineMeas side W line).pos pair.1) (tauLineProj_nonneg P W line pair.2)
   134	
   135	/-- Expanded line effects sum to the identity. This is the completeness
   136	obligation of `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
   137	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
   138	theorem expLineOp_sum_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   139	    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
   140	    ∑ f, S.expLineOp side W line f = 1 := by
   141	  let A : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) × DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) →
   142	      Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) := fun pair =>
   143	    heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect pair.1)
   144	      (tauLineProj P W line pair.2)
   145	  let g : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) × DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) →
   146	      DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) := fun pair => pair.1 + pair.2
   147	  calc
   148	    (∑ f, S.expLineOp side W line f) =
   149	        ∑ f, ∑ pair ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun pair => g pair = f), A pair := rfl
   150	    _ = ∑ pair, A pair := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ g A
   151	    _ = heteroKron (∑ x, (S.lineMeas side W line).effect x)
   152	        (∑ y, tauLineProj P W line y) := by
   153	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   154	      exact (heteroKron_sum_sum _ _).symm
   155	    _ = 1 := by
   156	      rw [(S.lineMeas side W line).sum_eq_one, sum_tauLineProj_eq_one]
   157	      exact heteroKron_one_one
   158	
   159	/-- The concrete expanded line measurement exhibited in the proof of
   160	`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`. Paper
   161	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`, blueprint
   162	`def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
   163	noncomputable def lineMeasExp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   164	    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
   165	    Measurement (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
   166	      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   167	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (S.expLineOp side W line)
   168	    (S.expLineOp_nonneg side W line) (S.expLineOp_sum_eq_one side W line)

   170	/-- The effects of the expanded line measurement are the convolution
   171	operators. -/
   172	@[simp] theorem lineMeasExp_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   173	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   174	    (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
   175	    (S.lineMeasExp side W line).effect f = S.expLineOp side W line f := rfl

   177	/-- The fine product measurement underlying the convolution definition of an
   178	expanded line measurement. Its outcome records the strategy and Pauli line
   179	polynomials separately. Paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
   180	noncomputable def lineTauMeas (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   181	    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
   182	    Measurement (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   183	      DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   184	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   185	    (fun p => heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect p.1)
   186	      ((tauLineMeas P W line).effect p.2))
   187	    (fun p => Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
   188	      ((S.lineMeas side W line).pos p.1) ((tauLineMeas P W line).pos p.2))
   189	    (by
   190	      change ∑ p : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   191	          DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d),
   192	          heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect p.1)
   193	            (tauLineProj P W line p.2) = 1
   194	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   195	      calc
   196	        (∑ x, ∑ y, heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect x)
   197	            (tauLineProj P W line y)) =
   198	            heteroKron (∑ x, (S.lineMeas side W line).effect x)

   204	/-- Effects of the fine product measurement are the corresponding Kronecker
   205	products of strategy and Pauli line effects. -/
   206	@[simp] theorem lineTauMeas_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   207	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   208	    (p : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) × DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
   209	    (S.lineTauMeas side W line).effect p =
   210	      heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect p.1)

   212	
   213	/-- The expanded line measurement is the addition postprocessing of its fine
   214	strategy--Pauli product measurement. This is the data-processing presentation
   215	used in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
   216	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
   217	theorem lineMeasExp_effect_eq_lineTauMeas_postprocess
   218	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind)
   219	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
   220	    (S.lineMeasExp side W line).effect f =
   221	      ((S.lineTauMeas side W line).postprocess
   222	        (fun p => p.1 + p.2)).effect f := by
   223	  change S.expLineOp side W line f = _
   224	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   225	  rfl

   227	/-- An expanded line effect is idempotent: the strategy line projectors and
   228	the Pauli line projectors are both orthogonal families, so distinct
   229	convolution terms annihilate one another. This is the projectivity
   230	calculation of `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
   231	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
   232	private theorem expLineOp_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   233	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   234	    (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
   235	    S.expLineOp side W line f * S.expLineOp side W line f =
   236	      S.expLineOp side W line f := by
   237	  have hM := S.lineMeas_isProjective side W line
   238	  unfold expLineOp
   239	  set s := Finset.univ.filter
   240	    (fun pair : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   241	        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) => pair.1 + pair.2 = f) with hs
   242	  let K : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   243	      DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   244	    fun p => heteroKron ((S.lineMeas side W line).effect p.1)
   245	      (tauLineProj P W line p.2)
   246	  change (∑ p ∈ s, K p) * (∑ q ∈ s, K q) = ∑ p ∈ s, K p
   247	  calc
   248	    (∑ p ∈ s, K p) * (∑ q ∈ s, K q) = ∑ p ∈ s, ∑ q ∈ s, K p * K q := by
   249	      rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   250	      simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   251	    _ = ∑ p ∈ s, ∑ q ∈ s, if q = p then K p else 0 := by
   252	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun q _ => ?_
   253	      simp only [K]
   254	      rw [heteroKron_mul]
   255	      by_cases hqp : q = p
   256	      · subst hqp
   257	        rw [if_pos rfl, (hM q.1).isIdempotentElem.eq,
   258	          tauLineProj_mul_tauLineProj, if_pos rfl]
   259	      · rw [if_neg hqp]
   260	        by_cases h1 : p.1 = q.1
   261	        · have h2 : p.2 ≠ q.2 := fun h2 => hqp (Prod.ext h1.symm h2.symm)
   262	          rw [tauLineProj_mul_tauLineProj, if_neg h2, heteroKron_zero_right]
   263	        · rw [DistanceCalculus.projective_effect_mul_effect_eq_zero _ hM h1,
   264	            heteroKron_zero_left]
   265	    _ = ∑ p ∈ s, K p := by
   266	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p hp => ?_
   267	      simp [hp]
   268	
   269	/-- The expanded line measurement is projective. This is the projectivity
   270	assertion in `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
   271	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
   272	theorem lineMeasExp_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   273	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
   274	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.lineMeasExp side W line) := by
   275	  intro f
   276	  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   277	  · change S.expLineOp side W line f * S.expLineOp side W line f =
   278	      S.expLineOp side W line f
   279	    exact expLineOp_mul_self S side W line f
   280	  · change star (S.expLineOp side W line f) = S.expLineOp side W line f
   281	    rw [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]

   288	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
   289	theorem expLineOp_zero_of_not_deg_d (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)

   300	      intro h2
   301	      apply hf
   302	      intro i hi
   303	      rw [← hsum, Pi.add_apply, h1 i hi, h2 i hi, add_zero]

     3	/-!
     4	# Evaluation of line polynomials at a sampled point
     5	
     6	This module records the elementary calculus of the partial evaluation
     7	`evalOpt` of a coefficient-list line polynomial at a point: the evaluation of
     8	a sum is the sum of the evaluations whenever both summands evaluate, a summand
     9	of an evaluating sum evaluates whenever the other summand does, the value is
    10	unique, and nothing evaluates at a point off the line. These facts underlie
    11	the manipulation of the evaluation classes in items 2 and 3 of the
    12	expanded-line consistency lemma.
    13	
    14	Every declaration below is a formalization-only auxiliary: the source uses
    15	these facts about evaluation without stating them.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	The evaluation classes `[eval_u(·) = a]` are `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. They are
    21	manipulated in `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons` and `eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2`,
    22	paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    30	
    31	/-- Coefficient-list evaluation is additive in the coefficient list. This
    32	is the additivity behind the convolution of `def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
    33	theorem evalCoefficient_add {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ} (c d : Fin n → K)
    34	    (t : K) : evalCoefficient (c + d) t = evalCoefficient c t + evalCoefficient d t := by
    35	  unfold evalCoefficient
    36	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    37	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    38	  rw [Pi.add_apply, add_mul]
    39	
    40	/-- A line polynomial has at most one value at a point of the line: if it
    41	evaluates both to `a` and to `b`, then `a = b`. -/
    42	theorem EvaluatesTo.unique {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} {line : LineDesc L}
    43	    {f : DegPoly L c} {u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L} {a b : ScalarQ L}
    44	    (ha : EvaluatesTo line f u a) (hb : EvaluatesTo line f u b) : a = b := by
    45	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := ha.1
    46	  rw [← ha.2 t ht, ← hb.2 t ht]
    47	
    48	/-- The sum of two evaluating line polynomials evaluates to the sum of
    49	their values. This is why the convolution outcome `f = f' + f''` evaluates
    50	whenever both convolution factors do. -/
    51	theorem EvaluatesTo.add {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} {line : LineDesc L}
    52	    {f g : DegPoly L c} {u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L} {a b : ScalarQ L}
    53	    (hf : EvaluatesTo line f u a) (hg : EvaluatesTo line g u b) :
    54	    EvaluatesTo line (f + g) u (a + b) :=
    55	  ⟨hf.1, fun t ht => by rw [evalCoefficient_add, hf.2 t ht, hg.2 t ht]⟩
    56	
    57	/-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, the first summand evaluates to
    58	the difference of their values. This is the converse direction used to identify
    59	the convolution fibers of an evaluation class. -/
    60	theorem EvaluatesTo.left_of_add {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} {line : LineDesc L}
    61	    {f g : DegPoly L c} {u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L} {s b : ScalarQ L}
    62	    (hfg : EvaluatesTo line (f + g) u s) (hg : EvaluatesTo line g u b) :
    63	    EvaluatesTo line f u (s - b) :=
    64	  ⟨hfg.1, fun t ht => by
    65	    have h := hfg.2 t ht
    66	    rw [evalCoefficient_add, hg.2 t ht] at h
    67	    exact eq_sub_of_add_eq h⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The partial evaluation returns `some a` exactly when the polynomial
    70	evaluates to `a`. This is the characterization that makes `evalOpt` the total
    71	form of the evaluation classes of `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
    72	theorem evalOpt_eq_some_iff {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
    73	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) (a : ScalarQ L) :
    74	    evalOpt line u f = some a ↔ EvaluatesTo line f u a := by
    75	  constructor
    76	  · intro h
    77	    unfold evalOpt at h
    78	    by_cases hex : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a
    79	    · rw [dif_pos hex, Option.some_inj] at h
    80	      rw [← h]
    81	      exact Classical.choose_spec hex
    82	    · rw [dif_neg hex] at h
    83	      exact absurd h (by simp)
    84	  · exact WinImplications.evalOpt_eq_some_of_evaluatesTo line f u a
    85	
    86	/-- The partial evaluation returns `none` exactly when no value is
    87	determined. This is the outcome that completes the evaluation classes to a
    88	measurement, written `[eval_u(·) = ⊥]` in `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`. -/
    89	theorem evalOpt_eq_none_iff {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
    90	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) :
    91	    evalOpt line u f = none ↔ ¬ ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a := by
    92	  unfold evalOpt
    93	  split_ifs with hex <;> simp [hex]
    94	
    95	/-- The partial evaluation of a sum of two evaluating line polynomials is
    96	the sum of their values. -/
    97	theorem evalOpt_add_of_some {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} {line : LineDesc L}
    98	    {u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L} {f g : DegPoly L c} {a b : ScalarQ L}
    99	    (hf : evalOpt line u f = some a) (hg : evalOpt line u g = some b) :
   100	    evalOpt line u (f + g) = some (a + b) :=
   101	  (evalOpt_eq_some_iff line u _ _).mpr
   102	    (((evalOpt_eq_some_iff line u f a).mp hf).add
   103	      ((evalOpt_eq_some_iff line u g b).mp hg))
   104	
   105	/-- If a sum and its second summand evaluate, so does the first summand,
   106	with the difference of the two values. -/
   107	theorem evalOpt_left_of_add_some {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} {line : LineDesc L}
   108	    {u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L} {f g : DegPoly L c} {s b : ScalarQ L}
   109	    (hfg : evalOpt line u (f + g) = some s) (hg : evalOpt line u g = some b) :
   110	    evalOpt line u f = some (s - b) :=
   111	  (evalOpt_eq_some_iff line u _ _).mpr
   112	    (((evalOpt_eq_some_iff line u _ s).mp hfg).left_of_add
   113	      ((evalOpt_eq_some_iff line u g b).mp hg))
   114	
   115	/-- A point at which some line polynomial evaluates lies on the line. -/
   116	theorem mem_pointSet_of_evalOpt_eq_some {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ}
   117	    {line : LineDesc L} {u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L} {f : DegPoly L c}
   118	    {a : ScalarQ L} (h : evalOpt line u f = some a) : u ∈ line.pointSet :=
   119	  ((evalOpt_eq_some_iff line u f a).mp h).1
   120	
   121	/-- Off the line, no line polynomial evaluates, so every outcome falls in
   122	the `none` class. -/
   123	theorem evalOpt_eq_none_of_not_mem {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} {line : LineDesc L}
   124	    {u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L} (hu : u ∉ line.pointSet) (f : DegPoly L c) :
   125	    evalOpt line u f = none := by
   126	  rw [evalOpt_eq_none_iff]
   127	  rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
   128	  exact hu ha.1
   129	
   130	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Pauli-register line projectors
     6	
     7	This module constructs the projective measurement `tau^{W,line}` of one
     8	generalized-Pauli register whose outcome is the restriction to a canonical
     9	line of the low-degree encoding of the measured basis label. It records that
    10	the outcome projectors are orthogonal projections summing to the identity,
    11	that they are symmetric matrices (so that they act identically on either half
    12	of an EPR pair), and that on an axis-parallel line they vanish outside the
    13	embedded degree-`d` subspace.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The projectors are `tau^{W,line}_{f''}` of `def:expanded-line-measurement`,
    18	with paper source
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. Their
    20	perfect self-consistency on an EPR pair is the ancillary input to item 1 of
    21	`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    30	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    31	
    32	noncomputable section
    33	
    34	/-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding
    35	restricts to `f` on `line`. This is `tau^{W,line}_f` in the proof of
    36	`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
    37	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`, blueprint
    38	`def:expanded-line-measurement`. -/
    39	noncomputable def tauLineProj (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    40	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
    41	    Op (PauliRegister P) :=
    42	  ∑ h ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun h : PauliRegister P =>
    43	      restrictToLine P.toLdParams line (lowDegreeEncoding h) = f),
    44	    pauliProj W h
    45	
    46	/-- Pauli line projectors are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity of
    47	the ancillary measurement in `def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
    48	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
    49	theorem tauLineProj_nonneg (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    50	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
    51	    0 ≤ tauLineProj P W line f := by
    52	  classical
    53	  unfold tauLineProj
    54	  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun e _ => (posSemidef_pauliProj W e).nonneg
    55	
    56	/-- The line coarse-graining of the generalized Pauli projectors is a
    57	symmetric matrix. Symmetry is what makes the projector act identically on
    58	either half of an EPR pair, and hence is the hypothesis behind the perfect
    59	ancilla consistency used in `enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons`, paper
    60	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
    61	theorem tauLineProj_transpose (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    62	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
    63	    (tauLineProj P W line f)ᵀ = tauLineProj P W line f := by
    64	  classical
    65	  simp only [tauLineProj, Matrix.transpose_sum, pauliProj_transpose]
    66	
    67	/-- Pauli line projectors belonging to distinct line polynomials are
    68	orthogonal, while each projector is idempotent. This is the ancillary product
    69	calculation in `def:expanded-line-measurement` and item 1 of
    70	`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
    71	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-558`. -/
    72	theorem tauLineProj_mul_tauLineProj (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    73	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (f g : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
    74	    tauLineProj P W line f * tauLineProj P W line g =
    75	      if f = g then tauLineProj P W line f else 0 := by
    76	  classical
    77	  unfold tauLineProj
    78	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    79	  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    80	  by_cases hfg : f = g
    81	  · subst g
    82	    rw [if_pos rfl]
    83	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    84	    intro e he
    85	    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single e]
    86	    · rw [pauliProj_mul_pauliProj, if_pos rfl]
    87	    · intro e' he' hee'
    88	      rw [pauliProj_mul_pauliProj, if_neg hee'.symm]
    89	    · exact fun h => (h he).elim
    90	  · rw [if_neg hfg]
    91	    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    92	    intro e he
    93	    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    94	    intro e' he'
    95	    rw [pauliProj_mul_pauliProj, if_neg]
    96	    intro hee'
    97	    apply hfg
    98	    rw [← (Finset.mem_filter.mp he).2, ← (Finset.mem_filter.mp he').2, hee']
    99	
   100	/-- The line fibers partition the complete family of Pauli eigenspace
   101	projectors. This is the completeness of the ancillary measurement in
   102	`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
   103	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
   104	theorem sum_tauLineProj_eq_one (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   105	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
   106	    ∑ f, tauLineProj P W line f = 1 := by
   107	  classical
   108	  rw [show (∑ f, tauLineProj P W line f) =
   109	      ∑ e : PauliRegister P, pauliProj W e by
   110	    simp only [tauLineProj]
   111	    exact Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ
   112	      (fun e : PauliRegister P =>
   113	        restrictToLine P.toLdParams line (lowDegreeEncoding e))
   114	      (fun e => pauliProj W e)]
   115	  exact sum_pauliProj_eq_one W
   116	
   117	/-- The projective line measurement on one Pauli register obtained by
   118	measuring the generalized Pauli basis and restricting the low-degree encoding
   119	of the outcome to `line`. This is the ancillary measurement of
   120	`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
   121	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
   122	noncomputable def tauLineMeas (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   123	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) :
   124	    Measurement (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) (PauliRegister P) :=
   125	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (tauLineProj P W line) (tauLineProj_nonneg P W line)
   126	    (sum_tauLineProj_eq_one P W line)
   127	
   128	/-- The effects of the Pauli line measurement are the line projectors. -/
   129	@[simp] theorem tauLineMeas_effect (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   130	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) :
   131	    (tauLineMeas P W line).effect f = tauLineProj P W line f := rfl
   132	
   133	/-- On an axis-parallel line, Pauli line projectors vanish outside the
   134	embedded degree-`d` subspace, because every restricted low-degree encoding has
   135	degree at most `d` there. This is the ancillary half of the last assertion of
   136	`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
   137	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:552-556`. -/
   138	theorem tauLineProj_eq_zero_of_axis (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   139	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (haxis : line.kind = .axis)
   140	    (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) (hf : ¬ f.FitsDegree P.d) :
   141	    tauLineProj P W line f = 0 := by
   142	  classical
   143	  unfold tauLineProj
   144	  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   145	  intro e he
   146	  exfalso
   147	  apply hf
   148	  rw [← (Finset.mem_filter.mp he).2]
   149	  exact restrictToLine_lowDegreeEncoding_fitsDegree_of_axis P.toLdParams line
   150	    haxis e
   151	
   152	/-! ## Interaction with the point projectors -/
   153	
   154	/-- On a point of the line, Pauli line projectors of non-evaluating
   155	polynomials vanish: every restricted low-degree encoding evaluates there.
   156	Formalization-only auxiliary for items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
   157	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
   158	theorem tauLineProj_eq_zero_of_evalOpt_none (P : AdmissibleParams)
   159	    (W : PauliKind) (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   160	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (hu : u ∈ line.pointSet)
   161	    (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d)) (hf : evalOpt line u f = none) :
   162	    tauLineProj P W line f = 0 := by
   163	  classical
   164	  unfold tauLineProj
   165	  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   166	  intro e he
   167	  exfalso
   168	  have hev := evalOpt_restrictToLine_lowDegreeEncoding P.toLdParams line e u hu
   169	  rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp he).2] at hev
   170	  have hev' : evalOpt line u f = some (dotProduct e (indicatorVec u)) := hev
   171	  rw [hf] at hev'
   172	  exact absurd hev' (by simp)
   173	
   174	/-- A Pauli line projector followed by a Pauli point projector at a point of
   175	the line is the line projector when the line polynomial evaluates to the
   176	point value, and zero otherwise. This is the exact consistency
   177	`tau^{W,line}_{f''}` versus `tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)}` in items 2 and 3 of
   178	`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
   179	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
   180	theorem tauLineProj_mul_tauPointProj (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   181	    (line : LineDesc P.toLdParams) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   182	    (hu : u ∈ line.pointSet) (f : DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
   183	    (b : PauliScalar P) :
   184	    tauLineProj P W line f * ProjectiveSetting.tauPointProj W u b =
   185	      if evalOpt line u f = some b then tauLineProj P W line f else 0 := by
   186	  classical
   187	  unfold tauLineProj ProjectiveSetting.tauPointProj
   188	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   189	  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum, pauliProj_mul_pauliProj]
   190	  calc
   191	    (∑ e ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun e : PauliRegister P =>
   192	        restrictToLine P.toLdParams line (lowDegreeEncoding e) = f),
   193	        ∑ e' ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun e' : PauliRegister P =>
   194	          dotProduct e' (indicatorVec u) = b),
   195	          if e = e' then pauliProj W e else 0) =
   196	      ∑ e ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun e : PauliRegister P =>
   197	        restrictToLine P.toLdParams line (lowDegreeEncoding e) = f),
   198	        if evalOpt line u f = some b then pauliProj W e else 0 := by
   199	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun e he => ?_
   200	      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq]
   201	      have hev := evalOpt_restrictToLine_lowDegreeEncoding P.toLdParams line e u hu
   202	      rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp he).2] at hev
   203	      have hev' : evalOpt line u f = some (dotProduct e (indicatorVec u)) := hev
   204	      by_cases hb : evalOpt line u f = some b
   205	      · rw [if_pos hb, if_pos]
   206	        have hbe : dotProduct e (indicatorVec u) = b :=
   207	          Option.some.inj (hev'.symm.trans hb)
   208	        exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hbe⟩
   209	      · rw [if_neg hb, if_neg]

   997		There exists a function $\delta_Q(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the
   998		following holds. For every $x, z \in \F_q^m$ and
   999		$\hilb \in \{\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}, \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}\}$ there are
  1000		projective measurements $\{\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\}_{a,b \in \F_q}$ acting
  1001		on $\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$ such that:
  1002		\begin{enumerate}
  1003			\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random
  1004			$x, z \in \F_q^m$,
  1005			\begin{equation}
  1006				\label{eq:qld-q-self-cons}
  1007				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
  1008				\approx_{\delta_Q}
  1009				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
  1010			\end{equation}
  1011			\item (\textbf{Consistency with $\hat{M}$}) On average over uniformly
  1012			random $x, z \in \F_q^m$,
  1013			\begin{gather}
  1014				\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz}
  1015				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
  1016				\approx_{\delta_Q}
  1017				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a} \,
  1018				\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
  1019				\\
  1020				\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx}
  1021				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
  1022				\approx_{\delta_Q}
  1023				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b} \,
  1024				\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
  1025			\end{gather}
  1026		\end{enumerate}
  1027		Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations also hold.
  1028		The operators $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a}$ and
  1029		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b}$ do not commute in general, so the
  1030		products in \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz} and
  1031		\eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} differ and the two relations are separate

  1034	\begin{proof}
  1035		\leanok
  1036		\uses{lem:qld-comm-cons, lem:qld-win-implications-obs,
  1037			def:combined-point-sandwich, lem:combined-point-commutation,
  1038			lem:combined-point-sandwich-comparisons,
  1039			lem:combined-point-sandwich-consistency, lem:combined-point-sandwich-rounding,

  1041			def:expanded-observables, lem:cancellation, fact:add-a-proj,
  1042			fact:agreement, lem:ortho-explicit-constant,
  1043			lem:distance-averaged-square-root, fact:triangle,
  1044			def:expanded-state, def:symmetric-equivalents}
  1045		We give the direct field-valued construction of
  1046		\cite{gap:qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation}. For fixed $(x,z)$ and
  1047		opposite placements $i=1,2$, abbreviate the expanded point projectors
  1048		by $X_{i,a}$ and $Z_{i,b}$. Set
  1049		$R_{i,a,b}=Z_{i,b}X_{i,a}Z_{i,b}$ for $a,b\in\F_q$.
  1050		These effects are positive and sum to the identity by projectivity and
  1051		completeness. Write $[A,B]=AB-BA$, and let $U_{i,r},V_{i,s}$ be the
  1052		expanded $X$ and $Z$ observables at $x,z$. The Fourier formulas in
  1053		Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-measurement}, together with character
  1054		orthogonality (Lemma~\ref{lem:cancellation}), give Parseval's identity
  1055		\[
  1056			\sum_{a,b}\|[X_{i,a},Z_{i,b}]\ket{\hat\psi}\|^2
  1057			=\E_{r,s}\|[U_{i,r},V_{i,s}]\ket{\hat\psi}\|^2.
  1058		\]
  1059		The observable commutator is the original twisted commutator tensored
  1060		with a unitary Pauli operator, so Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications-obs}
  1061		bounds its average by $O(\sqrt\eps)$ with no field-size factor.
  1062	
  1063		Put $D^X_a=X_{1,a}-X_{2,a}$, $D^Z_b=Z_{1,b}-Z_{2,b}$ and
  1064		$W_b=Z_{1,b}Z_{2,b}$. Expanding squared distances for projective
  1065		measurements twice gives the exact defect identity
  1066		\[
  1067			1-\sum_{a,b}\bra{\hat\psi}R_{1,a,b}R_{2,a,b}\ket{\hat\psi}
  1068			=\frac12\sum_b\|D^Z_b\ket{\hat\psi}\|^2
  1069			+\frac12\sum_{a,b}\|D^X_aW_b\ket{\hat\psi}\|^2.
  1070		\]
  1071		Opposite placements commute, and hence
  1072		$D^X_aW_b=W_bD^X_a+Z_{2,b}[X_{1,a},Z_{1,b}]
  1073		-Z_{1,b}[X_{2,a},Z_{2,b}]$.
  1074		Projective contraction (Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}) and the squared
  1075		three-term triangle inequality bound this defect by a nonnegative
  1076		$c_{x,z}$ with
  1077		$\E_{x,z}c_{x,z}\leq C(\eps+\sqrt\eps)$ for a universal $C\geq1$:
  1078		the two commutator sums cost $O(\sqrt\eps)$, while point
  1079		self-consistency from Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons} costs $O(\eps)$.
  1080	
  1081		Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:ortho-explicit-constant} on each point pair to
  1082		the two sandwich POVMs, first in the bipartition
  1083		$AA'\mid BA''(B'B'')$ and then in $BA''\mid AA'(B'B'')$.
  1084		It produces projective measurements $\hat Q^{x,z}$ on each player's
  1085		original expanded local space with squared distance at most
  1086		$220c_{x,z}^{1/4}$ from the sandwich. Applying
  1087		Lemma~\ref{lem:distance-averaged-square-root} twice gives
  1088		$\E c^{1/4}\leq(\E c)^{1/4}$, so the average squared rounding error is
  1089		at most $220[C(\eps+\sqrt\eps)]^{1/4}$.
  1090		The crosswise exchange $A'\leftrightarrow B''$, $A''\leftrightarrow B'$
  1091		fixes the expanded state and transfers these bounds to $AB''$ and
  1092		$BB'$ without a symmetry assumption on the strategy.
  1093	
  1094		Finally, $R_i-Z_iX_i=Z_i[X_i,Z_i]$ bounds the squared distance from
  1095		the sandwich to $Z_iX_i$ by $O(\sqrt\eps)$. Moving each factor to
  1096		the opposite placement using point self-consistency gives squared
  1097		distance $O(\eps)$ from $Z_iX_i$ to $X_jZ_j$.
  1098		The triangle inequality, with one further commutation for the other
  1099		product order, gives all three conclusions for every directed opposite
  1100		pair. For $0\leq\eps\leq1$, their errors are bounded by
  1101		$K\eps^{1/8}$ for a universal $K$. For $\eps>1$, projective
  1102		measurements and both ordered-product families satisfy
  1103		$\sum_{a,b}A_{a,b}^{\dagger}A_{a,b}\leq\Id$, so their squared
  1104		distances on a unit vector are at most $4$. Enlarging $K$ to at least
  1105		$4$ covers this regime as well. Thus $\delta_Q(\eps)=K\eps^{1/8}$
  1106		has the required polynomial bound on the whole nonnegative half-line.
  1107	\end{proof}

    20	isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$.
    21	We write $q = 2^t$ (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) and

    23	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
    24	(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-measurement}), their binary refinements

    26		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r}_b
    27		= \sum_{a \,:\, \tr(ar) = b} \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\,,
    28		\qquad r \in \F_q,\ b \in \F_2

    30	(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-trace-projection}), and the lines
    31	measurements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{f}$
    32	(Definition~\ref{def:expanded-line-measurement}) are those constructed in

    38	A subscript such as $(\,\cdot\,)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}$ indicates the pair of
    39	registers on which an operator acts; the two bipartitions in use are

    70	\section{Combined point measurements}
    71	
    72	The measurements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}$ and
    73	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}$ commute only approximately. The first goal of
    74	this chapter is to construct a single projective measurement that
    75	simultaneously measures both, first at points and then along lines. The
    76	source construction of the combined point measurement proceeds in three steps: the
    77	binary refinements $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}$ and
    78	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}$ are combined into a sandwich POVM, the
    79	resulting family is shown to satisfy an approximate linearity in the index
    80	pair $(r,s)$, and the following result of Natarajan and
    81	Vidick~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity} converts approximate linearity into exact
    82	linearity, from which a projective measurement with outcomes in $\F_q^2$ is
    83	obtained by Fourier averaging. The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} below
    84	instead forms the sandwich directly with field-valued outcomes and applies
    85	orthonormalization on the original expanded spaces. Parseval's identity
    86	transfers the commutation estimate without a field-size loss, so this argument
    87	does not use quantum linearity or further zero-state padding; the replacement
    88	is explained in \cite{gap:qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation}. We retain the
    89	linearity theorem and its source application separately.

    27	/-- The squared norm of `M ψ` is the quadratic form of `Mᴴ M`. -/
    28	private theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_sq_eq {ι : Type*}
    29	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    30	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    31	    ‖applyOperatorToState M ψ‖ ^ 2 =
    32	      (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (Mᴴ * M) ψ)).re := by
    33	  rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]
    34	  unfold applyOperatorToState
    35	  rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
    36	  change (inner ℂ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ) (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ)).re =
    37	    (inner ℂ ψ ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin M).adjoint (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ))).re
    38	  rw [LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right]

    40	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for Fact 4.20: evaluation in a fixed
    41	vector preserves operator order. -/
    42	theorem quadratic_form_mono {ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    {S T : Op ι} (hST : S ≤ T) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    45	    (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState S v)).re ≤
    46	      (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState T v)).re := by
    47	  have hpsd : (T - S).PosSemidef := Matrix.le_iff.mp hST
    48	  have hnonneg := hpsd.dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg v
    49	  have hdiff : 0 ≤ (inner ℂ v (applyOperatorToState (T - S) v)).re := by
    50	    simp only [applyOperatorToState, Matrix.toEuclideanLin,
    51	      Matrix.toLpLin_apply, EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
    52	    rw [dotProduct_comm]
    53	    exact (Complex.nonneg_iff.mp hnonneg).1
    54	  rw [show T = S + (T - S) by abel]
    55	  simp only [applyOperatorToState, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply, inner_add_right,
    56	    Complex.add_re]
    57	  exact le_add_of_nonneg_right hdiff

    72	/-- Finite-subset form of contraction by square-summable left multipliers. -/
    73	private theorem finset_sum_norm_mul_apply_le {γ ι : Type*}
    74	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    75	    (s : Finset γ) (C : γ → Op ι) (D : Op ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)
    76	    (hC : ∑ c ∈ s, (C c)ᴴ * C c ≤ 1) :
    77	    ∑ c ∈ s, ‖applyOperatorToState (C c * D) v‖ ^ 2 ≤
    78	      ‖applyOperatorToState D v‖ ^ 2 := by
    79	  calc
    80	    ∑ c ∈ s, ‖applyOperatorToState (C c * D) v‖ ^ 2 =
    81	        ∑ c ∈ s,
    82	          (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState D v)
    83	            (applyOperatorToState ((C c)ᴴ * C c)
    84	              (applyOperatorToState D v))).re := by
    85	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    86	          intro c _
    87	          rw [applyOperatorToState_mul]
    88	          exact norm_applyOperatorToState_sq_eq (C c) _
    89	    _ = (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState D v)
    90	          (applyOperatorToState (∑ c ∈ s, (C c)ᴴ * C c)
    91	            (applyOperatorToState D v))).re := by
    92	          simp [applyOperatorToState]
    93	    _ ≤ (inner ℂ (applyOperatorToState D v)
    94	          (applyOperatorToState (1 : Op ι) (applyOperatorToState D v))).re :=
    95	      quadratic_form_mono hC _
    96	    _ = ‖applyOperatorToState D v‖ ^ 2 := by
    97	      simpa [applyOperatorToState] using
    98	        (norm_applyOperatorToState_sq_eq (1 : Op ι) (applyOperatorToState D v)).symm

   194	\section{The source assertion and the two routes}
   195	
   196	The source proof in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} constructs $\hat Q^{\ell}_f$ by
   197	averaging, over a distribution $D$ on tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$
   198	provided by its sub-line lemma, the pushforward of
   199	$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ along a combining map, and reduces the lemma to a
   200	bound on the scalar consistency defect
   201	\begin{equation}
   202	  \Lambda \,=\,
   203	  \E_{(\ell,\ell_X,\ell_Z) \sim D}\
   204	  \E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta) \in \ell}
   205	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   206	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   207	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   208	  \ket{\hat\psi}\,,
   209	  \tag{\path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}}
   210	\end{equation}
   211	in which the point $(x,z,\alpha,\beta)$ is uniform on $\ell$ and the sum
   212	ranges over pairs of line polynomials.  The proof then bounds $\Lambda$
   213	twice, by different routes and with different results, and the printed
   214	record is internally inconsistent: the display introducing $\Lambda$
   215	asserts the first-route bound, while the closing lines assert the
   216	second-route bound as the operative one; the lemma statement claims a
   217	third form matching neither.
   218	
   219	\paragraph{The first route.}
   220	Three claims are chained.  The combined point measurement
   221	$\hat Q^{x,z}$ is replaced by the ordered product of the two point
   222	measurements at cost $\delta_Q^{1/2}$; the $X$-point factor is removed at
   223	cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$; and the remaining $Z$-point
   224	correlation is shown to be within
   225	$\sqrt{m}\,(\delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} + \eps^{1/4})$ of one.  The
   226	factors of $m$ enter through the mixture structure of the sub-line
   227	distribution: each restricted line distribution carries mixture weight
   228	$1/(2m)$ in the line-point distribution, so an average bounded by
   229	$\delta$ over the full distribution is bounded only by $2m\delta$ over a
   230	restricted component and by $4m^2\delta$ over a product of two
   231	components, and the Cauchy--Schwarz steps halve the exponents.  Chaining
   232	the claims gives
   233	\begin{equation*}
   234	  \Lambda \,=\, O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   235	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)
   236	  \,=\, m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)\,.
   237	\end{equation*}
   238	One intermediate assertion needs a harmless correction: the final line
   239	of the proof of the second claim asserts the bound
   240	$O(m^2 \delta_{\mathrm{Line}})$ for a consistency term that is close to
   241	one, rather than for its deficit.  Read as a bound on the deficit ---
   242	which is what the surrounding Cauchy--Schwarz argument requires and what
   243	the invoked line--point consistency provides after the mixture
   244	inflation --- the claim and its use are correct, with the square root of
   245	the deficit giving the stated cost $m\,\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}$.
   246	
   247	\paragraph{The second route.}
   248	After the chain, the source restarts: it asserts that, by Property~2 of
   249	its sub-line lemma, $\Lambda$ is a mixture, over types
   250	$\mathrm{v}_1, \mathrm{v}_2 \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and
   251	indices $i, j \in \{1, \dots, m\}$, of terms
   252	\begin{equation*}
   253	  \E_{(\ell_X, x) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_1,i}}\
   254	  \E_{(\ell_Z, z) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_2,j}}
   255	  \sum_{f_X,f_Z} \bra{\hat\psi}
   256	  \big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \ot
   257	  \big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
   258	  \ket{\hat\psi}
   259	\end{equation*}
   260	over two \emph{independently} sampled restricted line-point pairs,
   261	bounds each term by $O(m^2\delta_P)$ using the restricted-distribution
   262	consequence of the two-basis line lemma, and concludes
   263	$\Lambda = O(m^2\delta_P)$.  The invoked decomposition concerns the
   264	\emph{joint} law of the pair $((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z))$, where $x$ and
   265	$z$ are the two blocks of the single point sampled on $\ell$.  Property~2
   266	of the sub-line lemma does not assert this joint law: it asserts the
   267	component-wise product law of the pair of \emph{lines}
   268	$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, and the conditional uniformity of each point on its
   269	line separately --- equivalently, the laws of the two pairs
   270	$((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z'))$ and $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, z))$ in which
   271	the \emph{other} point is resampled independently.  These marginal
   272	statements are exactly what the first route's claims consume, each
   273	involving one point at a time; the joint decomposition used by the
   274	second route is a strictly stronger property and is not established by
   275	the lemma it is attributed to.

   277	\section{Why neither route yields the stated form}
   278	
   279	The stated error form is $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, a function of the two
   280	quantities $m^2\eps$ and $md/q$ that vanishes as both vanish.  The
   281	first-route bound is not dominated by any such function: along the
   282	scaling $\eps = m^{-4}$ with $q/(md) \to \infty$, both $m^2\eps = m^{-2}$
   283	and $md/q$ tend to $0$, while the term $m\,\eps^{1/4} = 1$ does not.
   284	Hence the established derivation supports no bound of the claimed form.
   285	The second-route bound, even granting the missing decomposition, carries
   286	the separate prefactor $m^2$: writing $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$
   287	with some fixed positive exponents, the contribution
   288	$m^2 (md/q)^{c}$ is not dominated by any vanishing function of $m^2\eps$
   289	and $md/q$, as the scaling $\eps = 0$, $md/q = m^{-2/c}$ shows, and the
   290	$\eps$-contribution fails similarly for sublinear exponents.  Neither
   291	observation asserts that the \emph{conclusion} of the lemma is false for
   292	some error function of the claimed form; the defect is that the printed
   293	proof does not deliver it.
   294	
   295	For orientation, the algebraic identity
   296	$m\,\eps^{1/2} = (m^2\eps)^{1/2}$ shows what a derivation of the claimed
   297	$\eps$-dependence would need: a chain that loses only square roots in the
   298	$\eps$-type quantities \emph{after} the restricted-distribution
   299	inflation would produce terms of the shape $(m^2\eps)^{1/2}$.  The
   300	printed chain loses fourth roots, through two nested Cauchy--Schwarz
   301	steps applied to already square-rooted quantities, and its
   302	$md/q$-dependence enters as $m\,\delta_P^{1/4}$, which the claimed form
   303	cannot absorb.

    47	
    48	\section{Key theorem forms}
    49	
    50	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    51	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    52	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    53	correlation estimate
    54	\[
    55	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    56	  \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(
    57	    O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    58	\]
    59	Its Fourier--Naimark argument produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector
    60	$\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying,
    61	with
    62	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    63	\[
    64	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    65	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    66	\]
    67	Moreover,
    68	\[
    69	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    70	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    71	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq2\delta.
    72	\]
    73	Equivalently, if $d^{\mathrm{bin}}_{\rho'}$ denotes the distance between the
    74	binary projective measurements associated with the two observables, then
    75	\[
    76	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    77	  d^{\mathrm{bin}}_{\rho'}(L^u,O^u\otimes I_{H'})^2\leq\delta.
    78	\]
    79	The provider prints $\delta$ for the first, operator-distance bound.  Its
    80	calculation instead proves the second, measurement-distance bound, which is
    81	one half of the squared operator distance.  The factor-of-two discrepancy and
    82	a counterexample to the printed operator bound are given in
    83	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex}, tracked in
    84	\ghissue{124}.
    85	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    86	observable is invertible.
    87	
    88	The source argument uses a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    89	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  If $\delta_{x,z}$ is the mean
    90	squared multiplicative defect on that fiber, the corresponding correlation
    91	error is $\delta_{x,z}/2$.  The corrected theorem therefore gives mean squared
    92	operator distance at most $\delta_{x,z}$, equivalently mean squared binary-
    93	measurement distance at most $\delta_{x,z}/2$.  Since the theorem accepts the
    94	actual nonnegative error on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber error is at
    95	most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still formulate
    96	the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space uniform over
    97	$(x,z)$.
    98	
    99	There is a different way to obtain the combined-point conclusion.  Let
   100	$q=2^t$ and let $\psi$ be the normalized state of a projective strategy
   101	winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$,
   102	with admissible field and degree parameters.  Its expanded state
   103	$\Psi=\hat\psi$ is $\psi$ on $AB$ tensored with maximally entangled states
   104	on $A'A''$ and $B'B''$, each ancillary register having dimension $q^M$,
   105	where $M=2^m$.  The opposite placement pairs are $AA',BA''$ and
   106	$BB',AB''$, in either direction; their operators commute because their
   107	registers are disjoint.  For operator families indexed by point pairs and
   108	outcomes define
   109	\[
   110	  D_\Psi^2(A,B)=\mathbb E_{x,z}\sum_{a,b\in\mathbb F_q}
   111	    \|(A^{x,z}_{a,b}-B^{x,z}_{a,b})\Psi\|^2.
   112	\]
   113	Write $X^x_{i,a}$ and $Z^z_{i,b}$ for the expanded field-valued point
   114	projectors on a placement $i$.  For each player one can construct projective
   115	measurements $Q^{x,z}$ on its original expanded local space such that, for
   116	every directed pair of opposite placements $i,j$,
   117	\[
   118	  D_\Psi^2(Q_i,Q_j),\quad
   119	  D_\Psi^2(Q_i,X_jZ_j),\quad
   120	  D_\Psi^2(Q_i,Z_jX_j)
   121	  \ \leq K\varepsilon^{1/8}.
   122	\]
   123	Here the products are indexed by $(a,b)$ and $K\geq1$ is universal,
   124	independent of the field, the point dimension, and the Hilbert-space
   125	dimensions.  This is the conclusion of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-10}, with an
   126	explicit admissible polynomial error; no common ancillary extension is assumed.
   127	
   128	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
   129	
   130	Lines~711--725 of
   131	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
   132	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
   133	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
   134	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
   135	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The
   136	quotation also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem
   137	and would unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect, and
   138	it appends the assertion at the identity, which follows from exact linearity as
   139	above.  These three are the differences between the quotation and the cited
   140	statement.
   141	
   142	The factor of two is not one of them.  The provider's equation~(3) proves the
   143	bound $\delta$ for binary-measurement distance; under the operator-distance
   144	convention displayed above this is the bound $2\delta$, and it is the
   145	provider's own Theorem~10 that prints $\delta$ for the operator distance.  The
   146	quotation states its conclusion in the relation $\approx_\delta$, which asserts
   147	only an $O(\delta)$ bound and therefore absorbs the constant factor instead of
   148	reproducing the erroneous one.  The normalization defect and its counterexample
   149	are the provider's and are treated in
   150	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex}.
   151	
   152	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
   153	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
   154	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
   155	many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
   156	to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
   157	
   158	The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
   159	with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
   160	returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
   161	one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
   162	orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
   163	observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
   164	chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
   165	or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.
   166	
   167	\section{Direct construction of the combined point measurement}
   168	
   169	The proof of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-10} in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}, mirrored at
   170	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:728--881}
   171	first forms a sandwich of binary refinements, rounds it, and then uses quantum
   172	linearity and Fourier inversion to recover field-valued outcomes.  The
   173	linearity application at lines~831--832 assumes sufficient zero ancillas.
   174	The following replacement starts with field-valued outcomes and uses the
   175	same orthonormalization principle without that application.
   176	
   177	\paragraph{Dimension-independent Parseval transfer.}
   178	Put $\chi(c)=(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(c)}$, where
   179	$\operatorname{tr}:\mathbb F_q\to\mathbb F_2$ is the field trace.  At a fixed
   180	point pair and placement, suppress $x,z,i$ and write $U_r,V_s$ for the
   181	expanded $X$ and $Z$ observables.  The Fourier formula for the expanded
   182	point effects, at source lines~384--418, is
   183	$X_a=\mathbb E_r\chi(ar)U_r$ and $Z_b=\mathbb E_s\chi(bs)V_s$.
   184	With $[A,B]=AB-BA$, character orthogonality gives
   185	\[
   186	 \sum_{a,b}\|[X_a,Z_b]\Psi\|^2
   187	 =\sum_{a,b}\left\|\frac{1}{q^2}\sum_{r,s}
   188	       \chi(ar+bs)[U_r,V_s]\Psi\right\|^2
   189	 =\mathbb E_{r,s}\|[U_r,V_s]\Psi\|^2.
   190	\]
   191	Indeed the sum over $(a,b)$ of the product of two character coefficients is
   192	$q^2$ when $(r,s)=(r',s')$ and zero otherwise.  This cancels two of the four
   193	inverse powers of $q$ from the squared Fourier normalization, leaving the
   194	uniform average, not an unnormalized sum.  The expanded observable
   195	commutator is the original twisted commutator tensored with a unitary Pauli
   196	operator.  Appending the normalized EPR pairs preserves its norm.  The
   197	estimate used in Lemma~\path{lem:qld-comm-cons}, source lines~466--505,
   198	therefore bounds the average of either side by $C\sqrt\varepsilon$ for a
   199	universal $C$.\footnote{The identities and the estimate are
   200	\path{sum_norm_place_expPointOp_commutator_sq} and
   201	\path{expPoint_comm} in
   202	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Commutation.lean}.}
   203	
   204	\paragraph{Sandwich consistency.}
   205	For fixed $(x,z)$ and opposite placements $1,2$, put
   206	$R_{i,a,b}=Z_{i,b}X_{i,a}Z_{i,b}$.  Positivity follows by writing each effect
   207	as $(X_{i,a}Z_{i,b})^\dagger(X_{i,a}Z_{i,b})$, and summing over $a$ and then
   208	$b$ gives the identity.  Opposite placements commute exactly.  Define
   209	$D^X_a=X_{1,a}-X_{2,a}$, $D^Z_b=Z_{1,b}-Z_{2,b}$,
   210	$W_b=Z_{1,b}Z_{2,b}$ and $K^i_{a,b}=[X_{i,a},Z_{i,b}]$.
   211	For projective measurements $P,Q$ and a vector $w$, expansion of the square
   212	gives
   213	$\sum_c\operatorname{Re}\langle w,P_cQ_cw\rangle
   214	=\|w\|^2-\frac12\sum_c\|(P_c-Q_c)w\|^2$.
   215	Applying this first to $X_1,X_2$ in $W_b\Psi$ and then to $Z_1,Z_2$ in
   216	$\Psi$ yields the exact consistency-defect identity
   217	\[
   218	  1-\sum_{a,b}\langle\Psi,R_{1,a,b}R_{2,a,b}\Psi\rangle
   219	  =\frac12\sum_b\|D^Z_b\Psi\|^2
   220	   +\frac12\sum_{a,b}\|D^X_aW_b\Psi\|^2.
   221	\]
   222	This is also the off-diagonal outcome mass, since both POVMs are complete.
   223	The decomposition
   224	$D^X_aW_b=W_bD^X_a+Z_{2,b}K^1_{a,b}-Z_{1,b}K^2_{a,b}$,
   225	the inequality $\|u+v-w\|^2\leq3(\|u\|^2+\|v\|^2+\|w\|^2)$, and
   226	projective contraction bound the defect by the nonnegative quantity
   227	\[
   228	 c_{x,z}=\frac12\sum_b\|D^Z_b\Psi\|^2
   229	  +\frac32\left(\sum_a\|D^X_a\Psi\|^2
   230	       +\sum_{a,b}\|K^1_{a,b}\Psi\|^2
   231	       +\sum_{a,b}\|K^2_{a,b}\Psi\|^2\right).
   232	\]
   233	Here $\sum_b W_b^\dagger W_b\leq I$ ensures that the first term in the
   234	decomposition does not incur an outcome-count factor.  Point
   235	self-consistency is $O(\varepsilon)$ and the Parseval estimate is
   236	$O(\sqrt\varepsilon)$, so
   237	$\mathbb E_{x,z}c_{x,z}\leq C_0(\varepsilon+\sqrt\varepsilon)$ for a
   238	universal $C_0\geq1$.\footnote{The exact identity, pointwise inequality,
   239	and average are proved in
   240	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Consistency.lean} as
   241	\path{sandwich_overlap_identity}, \path{sandwich_defect_pointwise_le}, and
   242	\path{avg_sandwichDefectBound_le}.  The function $c$ is
   243	\path{ProjectiveSetting.sandwichDefectBound}.}
   244	
   245	\paragraph{Rounding and averaging.}
   246	The explicit orthonormalization lemma says that two opposite POVMs of
   247	consistency defect at most $c\geq0$ admit a projective measurement on the
   248	first POVM's space with squared distance at most $220c^{1/4}$ from it.
   249	Apply it separately for each $(x,z)$, first with the bipartition
   250	$AA'\mid BA''(B'B'')$ and then with $BA''\mid AA'(B'B'')$.
   251	These are regroupings of the existing registers, not extensions.  Choose
   252	the resulting measurements for each point pair.  Two applications of the
   253	square-root averaging inequality give
   254	$\mathbb E c^{1/4}\leq(\mathbb E c)^{1/4}$, whence on each chosen placement
   255	\[
   256	 D_\Psi^2(Q_i,R_i)
   257	 \leq220\bigl[C_0(\varepsilon+\sqrt\varepsilon)\bigr]^{1/4}.
   258	\]
   259	The crosswise exchange $A'\leftrightarrow B''$, $A''\leftrightarrow B'$
   260	fixes the joint state of the two EPR pairs and the strategy state.  It carries these bounds to
   261	$AB''$ and $BB'$ without assuming symmetry of the strategy.\footnote{The
   262	rounding result is \path{projective_rounding_with_explicit_constant},
   263	blueprint \path{lem:ortho-explicit-constant}.  Its application and averaging
   264	are \path{exists_projective_close_sandwich} and
   265	\path{avgOver_rpow_quarter_le} in
   266	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Orthonormalization.lean}; the EPR
   267	exchange is in the neighboring \path{Placement.lean}.}
   268	
   269	\paragraph{The three conclusions and the error.}
   270	Since $R_i-Z_iX_i=Z_i[X_i,Z_i]$, projective contraction bounds
   271	$D_\Psi^2(R_i,Z_iX_i)$ by $O(\sqrt\varepsilon)$.
   272	Transporting the two factors separately to an opposite placement gives
   273	$D_\Psi^2(Z_iX_i,X_jZ_j)=O(\varepsilon)$: each move uses point
   274	self-consistency and square-summability of the other factor.  The triangle
   275	inequality along these comparisons, with one commutation for the other
   276	product order, proves all three desired distances with a universal multiple
   277	of
   278	$[C_0(\varepsilon+\sqrt\varepsilon)]^{1/4}
   279	 +\sqrt\varepsilon+\varepsilon$.
   280	For $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1$ this is bounded by
   281	$K\varepsilon^{1/8}$.  For $\varepsilon>1$, each relevant family has
   282	$\sum_a A_a^\dagger A_a\leq I$, so its squared distance from another such
   283	family on a unit vector is at most $4$.  Increasing $K$ to at least $4$
   284	proves the same bound for every possible error, including zero.\footnote{The
   285	ordered-product bounds are in
   286	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Sandwich.lean};
   287	\path{chain_bounds} and the scalar estimates are in
   288	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Closeness.lean}.  The conclusion is
   289	\path{exists_combinedPointsWitness} in
   290	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points.lean}.}
   291

   331	
   332	\section{Conclusion}
   333	
   334	The quotation changes averaged closeness to pointwise closeness, inserts an
   335	unnecessary upper bound on $\delta$, and appends an assertion at the identity
   336	that is derivable from exact linearity.  It does not reproduce the provider's
   337	factor-of-two normalization defect, since it states its conclusion in a
   338	relation that absorbs constant factors; that defect is the provider's own and
   339	is treated separately.  The single-family theorem is now
   340	proved with mean squared operator error at most $2\delta$, equivalently mean
   341	squared binary-measurement error at most $\delta$.  Its use for the family
   342	indexed by $(x,z)$ still requires an explicit finite common-extension argument.
   343	The combined-point theorem, however, is proved by a different, dimension-independent
   344	argument with error $K\varepsilon^{1/8}$ on the original expanded local spaces.
   345	There is no remaining statement discrepancy or proof obligation for that
   346	construction; the common-extension obligation belongs only to the unused
   347	linearity argument.
