    13	
    14	\begin{document}
    15	\maketitle
    16	
    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Once a cited statement is established to be mathematically false, the repair
   110	and escalation procedure is governed by Section~6 of
   111	\path{local/protocols/issues-prs.md}.  Before asking the human owner to choose a
   112	replacement, a dedicated mathematical-gap session must produce a correction
   113	which is correct, sufficient for every paper and blueprint use, and minimal,
   114	then iterate it against the Lean statement and its downstream consumers.  A
   115	Claude Fable~5.1 session is currently launched by the owner session through its
   116	Agent tool; a Codex main session requests that lane on progress log~\#27 rather
   117	than dispatching a Codex worker.  Only after the astra poller reports
   118	availability on owner inbox~\#26 does the Codex route become
   119	\texttt{dispatch.sh --role mathfix} with astra.  A change to a mathematical
   120	definition or game is escalated immediately; other repairs reach the owner
   121	inbox only after the shared convergence budget expires.
   122	
   123	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   124	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   125	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   126	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   127	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   128	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   129	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   130	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   131	implementation.
   132	
   133	\section{When to Write a Note}
   134	
   135	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   136	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   137	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   138	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   139	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   140	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   141	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   142	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   143	relation.
   144	
   145	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   146	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   147	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   148	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   149	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   150	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   151	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   152	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   153	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   154	
   155	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   156	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   157	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   158	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   159	
   160	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   161	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   162	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   163	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   164	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   165	though it were the paper theorem.
   166	
   167	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   168	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   169	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   170	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   171	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   172	argument.
   173	
   174	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   175	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   176	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   177	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   178	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   179	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   180	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   181	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   182	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   183	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   184	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   185	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   186	
   187	\section{Counterexamples}
   188	
   189	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   190	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   191	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   192	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   193	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.
   194	
   195	When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
   196	especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
   197	otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
   198	whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
   199	of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
   200	a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
   201	still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.
   202	
   203	\section{Revision of a Note}
   204	
   205	A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
   206	obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
   207	revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
   208	declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
   209	classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
   210	which point remains unsettled.
   211	
   212	Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
   213	rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
   214	mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
   215	the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
   216	discussion.
   217	
   218	\section{Form of the Note}
   219	
   220	Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant

    61	\section{Key theorem forms}
    62	
    63	Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple of the Pauli basis
    64	test, $\ket{\hat\psi}$ is the expanded state of the projective strategy
    65	under analysis, succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all
    66	approximations are with respect to $\ket{\hat\psi}$.  For lines
    67	$\ell_X, \ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$, the POVM $\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$,
    68	with outcomes pairs of polynomials of degree at most $md$ on the two
    69	lines, is the two-basis combined line measurement, and
    70	$\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is the combined point measurement; their
    71	consistency errors are $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$ and
    72	$\delta_Q = \poly(\eps)$ respectively, and
    73	$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}} = \poly(\eps)$ is the line--point consistency
    74	error of the strategy.  The lemma under discussion asserts that a
    75	measurement $\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, built for each line $\ell$ in
    76	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, is $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$-consistent, on average over
    77	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$, with the combined point
    78	measurement on the extended coordinates, together with the
    79	register-swapped counterpart.%
    80	\footnote{In the mirror of the source consulted here,
    81	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}: the
    82	lemma statement, with the error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, is at
    83	lines~1020--1034 (label \path{lem:qld-4-13}); the central display with
    84	the first-route bound at lines~1134--1137
    85	(label \path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}); the three claims at
    86	lines~1140--1239 (labels \path{claim:17-1}--\path{claim:17-3}); the
    87	second-route conclusion $O(m^2\delta_P)$ at lines~1241--1245, preceded by
    88	a duplicated sentence whose second copy carries a malformed reference;
    89	the product-distribution estimate invoked there at lines~1055--1061
    90	(label \path{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}); and the sub-line lemma at
    91	lines~1063--1116 (label \path{lem:qld-sublines}).}
    92	The comparison involves four forms of the error function
    93	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(\eps,m,d,q)$.
    94	\begin{enumerate}
    95	  \item \textbf{Source form.}
    96	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = \poly(m^2\eps,\, md/q)$.  This is the form
    97	  printed in the statement.  Neither printed derivation supports it.
    98	  \item \textbf{Established form (first route).}
    99	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}
   100	  = O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   101	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)$, a function of the form
   102	  $m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$.
   103	  \item \textbf{Second-route form (conditional).}
   104	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = O(m^2 \delta_P)
   105	  = m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$, conditional on a joint-law
   106	  decomposition that the sub-line lemma, as stated, does not provide.
   107	  \item \textbf{Consumer requirement.}  The unique consumer, the
   108	  polynomial-pair lemma, feeds $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$ into an error
   109	  of the form
   110	  $a(md)^a(\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ imported
   300	printed chain loses fourth roots, through two nested Cauchy--Schwarz
   301	steps applied to already square-rooted quantities, and its
   302	$md/q$-dependence enters as $m\,\delta_P^{1/4}$, which the claimed form
   303	cannot absorb.

   305	\section{Correction and alternative repairs}
   306	
   307	The first direction below is the one the blueprint adopts; the remaining
   308	directions are alternatives, none of which is claimed as established.
   309	
   310	\paragraph{Corrected error form (adopted in the proof).}
   311	The operative error form is
   312	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$ --- concretely,
   313	the first-route bound.  Following the proof-gap protocol, the source-labelled
   314	statement keeps its printed form and the correction is carried by the proof,
   315	by the chapter remark, and by a separate formalization-support node, rather
   316	than being substituted silently into the source statement.  The only consumer
   317	is the polynomial-pair lemma, whose imported error
   318	$a(md)^a(\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ absorbs
   319	$m^{O(1)}$ prefactors by enlarging $a$ and shrinking $b$.  The blueprint proof
   320	records this absorption and the corrected deficit reading of the second claim.
   321	Two obligations remain: carry out that absorption with explicit constants when
   322	the lemma is formalized, and prove the three chained estimates.
   323	
   324	\paragraph{Repairing the second route.}
   325	Strengthen Property~2 of the sub-line lemma to the joint product law: in
   326	each mixture component, the pairs $(\ell_X, x)$ and $(\ell_Z, z)$ are
   327	independent with the stated restricted-distribution laws.  The sampling
   328	procedure makes this plausible, since in each component the two pairs
   329	are built from disjoint collections of the independent ingredients (the
   330	two blocks of the uniform point, the direction blocks, and the fresh
   331	auxiliary choices).  Open obligations: (i)~state and prove the
   332	strengthened property for every component, including lines whose
   333	direction blocks vanish and degenerate to singletons; (ii)~re-derive the
   334	mixture decomposition of $\Lambda$ from the strengthened property;
   335	(iii)~note that even then the route delivers only
   336	$O(m^2\delta_P) = m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, so this direction removes
   337	the unsupported step of the printed proof but still requires the
   338	error-form decision of the previous direction, with $m^2$ in place of
   339	$m$.
   340	
   341	\paragraph{Establishing the claimed form.}
   342	Re-derive the chain so that every factor of $m$ enters jointly with
   343	$\eps$ as $m^2\eps$, in the sense of the orientation identity above.
   344	Open obligations: (i)~find a chaining that avoids one of the two nested
   345	square-root losses, or prove restricted-distribution versions of the
   346	underlying consistency lemmas directly at their inflated errors;
   347	(ii)~handle the $md/q$-dependence, since a residual term
   348	$m (md/q)^{c}$ is incompatible with the claimed form for the current
   349	exponents.  No derivation along these lines is known here, and the
   350	direction may be infeasible; in that case the corrected error form of
   351	the first direction stands.

     3	/-!
     4	# The sandwich POVM of the expanded point measurements
     5	
     6	The first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10` combines the two expanded point
     7	measurements into the sandwich POVM
     8	`R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^{(Point,Z),z}_b M^{(Point,X),x}_a M^{(Point,Z),z}_b`.  The
     9	source forms it from the binary refinements; here it is formed directly with
    10	outcomes in `F_q × F_q`, which the Parseval transfer of
    11	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Commutation.lean` makes possible.  This file
    12	defines the POVM, proves that it is close to the ordered product
    13	`M^Z_b M^X_a` by the approximate commutation, and records the consistency of
    14	the ordered products across opposite register placements, which follows from
    15	the self-consistency of each factor.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `ProjectiveSetting.sandwichPoint`: the sandwich POVM.
    20	* `sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le`: closeness of the sandwich to the ordered
    21	  product on every placement, with the error of `lem:qld-comm-cons`.
    22	* `ordered_cross_dist_le`: the ordered product on one placement is close to
    23	  the reversed ordered product on the opposite placement.
    24	
    25	## References
    26	
    27	Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-748`
    28	(the sandwich and display `eq:qld-r-2`), blueprint

    30	route is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`.
    31	-/

    46	/-- An expanded point effect is self-adjoint. -/
    47	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    48	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    49	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    50	    ((S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a)ᴴ = (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    51	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq
    52	
    53	/-- An expanded point effect is idempotent. -/
    54	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    55	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    56	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    57	    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
    58	      (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    59	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isIdempotentElem.eq
    60	
    61	/-- The sandwich `M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` is `(M^X_a M^Z_b)ᴴ (M^X_a M^Z_b)`. -/
    62	theorem sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    63	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a b : PauliScalar P) :
    64	    (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    65	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b =
    66	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b)ᴴ *
    67	        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b) := by
    68	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose,
    69	    pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _
    70	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b),
    71	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a)
    72	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a), pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self,
    73	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
    74	
    75	/-- The sandwich effects resolve the identity. -/
    76	theorem sum_sandwich_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    77	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    78	    ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
    79	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
    80	          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
    81	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 = 1 := by
    82	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
    83	  calc ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
    84	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    85	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b
    86	      = ∑ b : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b *
    87	          (∑ a : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a) *
    88	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b := by
    89	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
    90	        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
    91	    _ = 1 := by
    92	        simp_rw [(S.pointMeasExp side .X x).sum_eq_one, mul_one,
    93	          pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
    94	        exact (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).sum_eq_one
    95	
    96	/-- The sandwich POVM `R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` of the two expanded
    97	point measurements, with outcomes in `F_q × F_q`.  This is the POVM of the
    98	first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-736`,
   100	formed directly with field-valued outcomes rather than from the binary
   101	refinements; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`. -/
   102	def sandwichPoint (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   103	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   104	    Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   105	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   106	    (fun ab => (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   107	      (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
   108	      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2)
   109	    (fun ab => by
   110	      rw [sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   111	      exact Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   112	        (Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self _))
   113	    (sum_sandwich_eq_one S side x z)
   114	
   115	/-- The effects of the sandwich POVM. -/
   116	@[simp] theorem sandwichPoint_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   117	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   118	    (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) :
   119	    (S.sandwichPoint side x z).effect ab =
   120	      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   121	        (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
   122	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 := rfl
   123	
   124	/-- The sandwich differs from the ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` by
   125	`M^Z_b` times the commutator.  This is the algebra behind display
   126	`eq:qld-r-2`, paper
   127	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:737-742`. -/
   128	theorem sandwichPoint_effect_sub_ordered (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   129	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   130	    (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) :
   131	    (S.sandwichPoint side x z).effect ab -
   132	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   133	          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 =
   134	      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   135	        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
   136	            (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 -
   137	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
   138	            (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1) := by
   139	  rw [sandwichPoint_effect, mul_sub, ← Matrix.mul_assoc, ← Matrix.mul_assoc,
   140	    pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
   141	
   142	/-- The sandwich POVM is close to the ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` on every
   143	register placement, on average over the point pair, with the error of
   144	`lem:qld-comm-cons`.  This is display `eq:qld-r-2` of the proof of
   145	`lem:qld-4-10`, paper
   146	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:737-742`, with
   147	field-valued outcomes. -/
   148	theorem sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le :
   149	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
   150	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   151	        (p : Placement),
   152	        opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   153	          (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p
   154	            ((S.sandwichPoint p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   155	          (fun xz ab => S.place p
   156	            ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   157	              (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   158	          S.psiHat ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε := by
   159	  obtain ⟨C, hC, h⟩ := expPoint_comm
   160	  refine ⟨C, hC, fun P ε S p => le_trans ?_ (h P ε S p)⟩
   161	  unfold opFamilyDistSq
   162	  refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun xz => Finset.sum_le_sum fun ab _ => ?_
   163	  rw [← place_sub, sandwichPoint_effect_sub_ordered, place_mul,
   164	    DistanceCalculus.applyOperatorToState_mul, ← place_sub]
   165	  exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _)
   166	    (MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_le
   167	      (S.place_conjTranspose_mul_self_le_one p
   168	        (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective p.side .Z xz.2 ab.2)) _) 2
   169	
   170	/-- The ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` on one placement is close to the
   171	reversed ordered product `M^X_a M^Z_b` on the opposite placement, on average
   172	over the point pair, with the self-consistency error of `lem:qld-comm-cons`.
   173	The two factors are transported one at a time, each transport costing the
   174	self-consistency of that factor by `fact:add-a-proj`.  Paper
   175	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:743-770`
   176	(displays `eq:qld-rw-self-cons-2` and `eq:qld-rw-self-cons-3`), blueprint
   177	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:851-870`. -/
   178	theorem ordered_cross_dist_le :
   179	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
   180	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ) (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   181	        (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
   182	        opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   183	          (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p₁
   184	            ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   185	              (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   186	          (fun xz ab => S.place p₂
   187	            ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   188	              (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   189	          S.psiHat ≤ C * ε := by
   190	  obtain ⟨C, hC, h⟩ := expPoint_self_cons
   191	  refine ⟨4 * C, by linarith, ?_⟩
   192	  intro P ε S p₁ p₂ hopp
   193	  have hX := h P ε S p₁ p₂ hopp .X
   194	  have hZ := h P ε S p₁ p₂ hopp .Z
   195	  -- the middle family is `M^Z_b` on the first placement times `M^X_a` on the
   196	  -- second; each factor is transported by the self-consistency of that factor
   197	  have h₁ : opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   198	      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p₁
   199	        ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   200	          (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   201	      (fun xz ab => S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) *
   202	        S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   203	      S.psiHat ≤ C * ε := by
   204	    refine le_trans ?_ (le_of_eq_of_le (avgOver_uniform_fst
   205	      (β := Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   206	      (fun x => ∑ a : PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   207	        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X x).effect a) -
   208	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X x).effect a)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2)) hX)
   209	    unfold opFamilyDistSq
   210	    refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun xz => ?_
   211	    have hpt : ∀ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   212	        S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   213	            (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1) -
   214	          S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) *
   215	            S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1) =
   216	          S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) *
   217	            (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1) -
   218	              S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1)) := by
   219	      intro ab
   220	      rw [S.place_mul p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2)
   221	        ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1), mul_sub]
   222	    simp only [hpt, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   223	    refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => ?_
   224	    exact DistanceCalculus.sum_norm_mul_apply_le
   225	      (fun b => S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect b))
   226	      (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect a) -
   227	        S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect a)) S.psiHat
   228	      (measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one
   229	        (S.placedMeasurement p₁ (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2)))
   230	  have h₂ : opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
   231	      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
   232	        S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) *
   233	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   234	      (fun xz ab => S.place p₂
   235	        ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   236	          (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   237	      S.psiHat ≤ C * ε := by
   238	    refine le_trans ?_ (le_of_eq_of_le (avgOver_uniform_snd
   239	      (α := Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   240	      (fun z => ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ‖applyOperatorToState
   241	        (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z z).effect b) -
   242	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z z).effect b)) S.psiHat‖ ^ 2)) hZ)
   243	    unfold opFamilyDistSq
   244	    refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun xz => ?_
   245	    have hpt : ∀ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
   246	        S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) *
   247	            S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1) -
   248	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   249	            (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) =
   250	          S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1) *
   251	            (S.place p₁ ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) -
   252	              S.place p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2)) := by
   253	      intro ab
   254	      rw [S.place_mul p₂ ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1)
   255	        ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2),
   256	        S.place_comm p₁ p₂ hopp ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2)
   257	          ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1), ← mul_sub]
   258	    simp only [hpt, Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
   259	    refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ => ?_
   260	    exact DistanceCalculus.sum_norm_mul_apply_le

     8	# Witnesses for combining the Pauli bases
     9	
    10	This module defines the five measurement and distribution witnesses used in
    11	the combining argument.  Every measurement is indexed by the player side, so
    12	Alice's and Bob's local spaces remain distinct.  The extended-dimensional
    13	line objects use the directly indexed low-degree interface and therefore do
    14	not require a dimension-divisibility hypothesis.

    19	the measurement conclusions of `lem:qld-4-10`, `lem:qld-xz-lines`, and

    21	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`.  `SubLineWitness` and
    22	`ExtendedLinesWitness` instead support `lem:qld-sublines` and `lem:qld-4-13`

    38	
    39	/-- Identify the direct extended game's scalar field with the Pauli scalar
    40	field.  Both are selected by `fixedFieldModel`; only their proof argument for
    41	admissibility differs. -/
    42	noncomputable def extendedDirectScalarEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    43	    DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd ≃+* PauliScalar P := by
    44	  have h : P.extendedDirectLd.hq = P.hq := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    45	  cases h
    46	  exact RingEquiv.refl _
    47	
    48	/-- Transport an extended direct point into the canonical Pauli scalar field. -/
    49	def directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
    50	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m -> DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    51	    Fin (2 * P.m + 2) -> PauliScalar P :=
    52	  fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (u i)

    54	/-! ## Finite direct-line carrier -/
    55	
    56	/-- A finite code for directly indexed lines, omitting only proof fields. -/
    57	private abbrev DirectLineDescCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    58	  ((Fin D.m -> DirectScalarQ D) × Fin D.m) ⊕
    59	    ((Fin D.m -> DirectScalarQ D) × Fin D.m ×
    60	      (Fin D.m -> DirectScalarQ D))
    61	
    62	/-- Encode a directly indexed line by its tag and mathematical data. -/
    63	private def directLineDescCode (D : DirectLdParams) :
    64	    DirectLineDesc D -> DirectLineDescCode D
    65	  | .axis base index _ => .inl (base, index)
    66	  | .diagonal base index direction _ _ => .inr (base, index, direction)
    67	
    68	/-- The direct-line code is injective by proof irrelevance. -/
    69	private theorem directLineDescCode_injective (D : DirectLdParams) :
    70	    Function.Injective (directLineDescCode D) := by
    71	  intro line line' h
    72	  cases line with
    73	  | axis base index baseFixed =>
    74	      cases line' with
    75	      | axis base' index' baseFixed' =>
    76	          simp only [directLineDescCode, Sum.inl.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
    77	          rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    78	          rfl
    79	      | diagonal => simp [directLineDescCode] at h
    80	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero =>
    81	      cases line' with
    82	      | axis => simp [directLineDescCode] at h
    83	      | diagonal base' index' direction' baseFixed' prefixZero' =>
    84	          simp only [directLineDescCode, Sum.inr.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
    85	          rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
    86	          rfl

    88	/-- Directly indexed line descriptions form a finite type. -/
    89	noncomputable instance directLineDescFintype (D : DirectLdParams) :
    90	    Fintype (DirectLineDesc D) :=
    91	  Fintype.ofInjective (directLineDescCode D) (directLineDescCode_injective D)

    93	/-! ## Combined point and line measurements -/
    94	
    95	/-- Projective joint point measurements and their ordered consistency
    96	guarantees from `lem:qld-4-10`, paper lines 689--709.  The `XZ` and `ZX`
    97	products are retained as distinct fields. -/
    98	structure CombinedPointsWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    99	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (δ : ℝ) where
   100	  /-- The complete joint measurement on each player's expanded local space. -/
   101	  Q : (side : PlayerSide) ->
   102	    (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) ->
   103	    (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) ->
   104	    Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   105	  /-- Every joint point measurement is projective. -/
   106	  projective : ∀ side x z, Measurement.IsProjective (Q side x z)
   107	  /-- Joint point measurements agree across every directed opposite placement. -/
   108	  self_consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   109	    opFamilyDistSq
   110	      (uniformDistribution
   111	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   112	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   113	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2 ((Q p2.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   114	      S.psiHat <= δ
   115	  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `X`-then-`Z` product. -/
   116	  consistent_XZ : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   117	    opFamilyDistSq
   118	      (uniformDistribution
   119	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   120	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   121	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2
   122	        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   123	          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   124	      S.psiHat <= δ
   125	  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product. -/
   126	  consistent_ZX : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   127	    opFamilyDistSq
   128	      (uniformDistribution
   129	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   130	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   131	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2
   132	        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   133	          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))

+/-!
+# Closeness estimates for the combined point measurements
+
+Given projective measurements `Q^{x,z}` on each player's expanded local space
+that are close to the sandwich POVMs on the placements where they were
+constructed, this file assembles the three conclusions of `lem:qld-4-10` on
+every pair of opposite placements by the triangle inequality along
+`Q ≈ R ≈ M^Z M^X ≈ M^X M^Z` and the cross-placement consistency of the
+ordered products.  It also records the trivial bound `4` on the state-dependent
+distance of two square-summable families, used when the test error exceeds
+one, and the elementary estimate collapsing the error terms `ε`, `√ε`, and
+`(ε + √ε)^{1/4}` into a single power `ε^{1/8}` when `ε ≤ 1`.
+
+## References
+
+Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:838-881`
+(self-consistency and consistency with `M̂` in the proof of `lem:qld-4-10`),
+blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:803-960`; the route
+is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+

+

+/-! ## The trivial bound -/
+
+/-- The state-dependent distance of two square-summable families is at most
+`4` on a unit vector, under a uniform distribution. -/
+theorem opFamilyDistSq_uniform_le_four {X α ι : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
+    [Nonempty X] [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (A B : X → α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
+    (hA : ∀ x, ∑ a, (A x a)ᴴ * A x a ≤ 1) (hB : ∀ x, ∑ a, (B x a)ᴴ * B x a ≤ 1) :
+    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution X) A B ψ ≤ 4 := by
+  unfold opFamilyDistSq
+  calc avgOver (uniformDistribution X) (fun x =>
+        ∑ a, ‖applyOperatorToState (A x a - B x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
+      ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution X) (fun _ => (4 : ℝ)) := by
+        exact avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun x =>
+          sum_norm_sub_apply_sq_le_four (A x) (B x) ψ hψ (hA x) (hB x)
+    _ = 4 := avgOver_uniform_const _
+
+/-- The products `A_a B_b` of the effects of two projective measurements on a
+common space are square-summable to the identity. -/
+theorem sum_mul_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_one {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
+    [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (A : Measurement α ι) (B : Measurement β ι)
+    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
+    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
+    ∑ ab : α × β, (A.effect ab.1 * B.effect ab.2)ᴴ * (A.effect ab.1 * B.effect ab.2) =
+      1 := by
+  have hpt : ∀ (a : α) (b : β),
+      (A.effect a * B.effect b)ᴴ * (A.effect a * B.effect b) =
+        B.effect b * A.effect a * B.effect b := by
+    intro a b
+    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, (hA a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
+      (hB b).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _ (A.effect a * B.effect b),
+      ← Matrix.mul_assoc (A.effect a) (A.effect a), (hA a).isIdempotentElem.eq,
+      ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
+  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
+  calc ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α, (A.effect a * B.effect b)ᴴ * (A.effect a * B.effect b)
+      = ∑ b : β, B.effect b * (∑ a : α, A.effect a) * B.effect b := by
+        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
+        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
+        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hpt a b
+    _ = 1 := by
+        simp_rw [A.sum_eq_one, mul_one]
+        rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => (hB b).isIdempotentElem.eq]
+        exact B.sum_eq_one
+
+/-- The products `B_b A_a` of the effects of two projective measurements on a
+common space, indexed by the pair `(a, b)`, are square-summable to the
+identity. -/
+theorem sum_mul_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_one' {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α]
+    [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (A : Measurement α ι) (B : Measurement β ι)
+    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
+    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
+    ∑ ab : α × β, (B.effect ab.2 * A.effect ab.1)ᴴ * (B.effect ab.2 * A.effect ab.1) =
+      1 := by
+  have hpt : ∀ (a : α) (b : β),
+      (B.effect b * A.effect a)ᴴ * (B.effect b * A.effect a) =
+        A.effect a * B.effect b * A.effect a := by
+    intro a b
+    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, (hA a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
+      (hB b).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _ (B.effect b * A.effect a),
+      ← Matrix.mul_assoc (B.effect b) (B.effect b), (hB b).isIdempotentElem.eq,
+      ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
+  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+  calc ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β, (B.effect b * A.effect a)ᴴ * (B.effect b * A.effect a)
+      = ∑ a : α, A.effect a * (∑ b : β, B.effect b) * A.effect a := by
+        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
+        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hpt a b
+    _ = 1 := by
+        simp_rw [B.sum_eq_one, mul_one]
+        rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (hA a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
+        exact A.sum_eq_one

+/-! ## The chain of closeness estimates -/
+
+namespace ProjectiveSetting

+variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
+
+/-- The three closeness conclusions of `lem:qld-4-10` for a pair of projective
+families close to the placed sandwiches: with `η` the closeness of `Q` to `R`
+on every placement, `C₁ √ε` the closeness of `R` to the ordered product,
+`C₂ √ε` the commutation error, and `C₃ ε` the cross-placement consistency of
+the ordered products, the distances from `Q` on one placement to the two
+ordered products and to `Q` on the opposite placement are bounded by explicit
+combinations.  Paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:838-881`. -/
+theorem chain_bounds (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+    (Q : (side : PlayerSide) → PointPair P →
+      Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side))
+    (η C₁ C₂ C₃ : ℝ)
+    (hQR : ∀ p : Placement, opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
+        S.place p ((Q p.side xz).effect ab))
+      (fun xz ab => S.place p ((S.sandwichPoint p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
+      S.psiHat ≤ η)
+    (h₁ : ∀ p : Placement, opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
+        S.place p ((S.sandwichPoint p.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
+      (fun xz ab => S.place p
+        ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
+          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
+      S.psiHat ≤ C₁ * Real.sqrt ε)
+    (h₂ : ∀ p : Placement, opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p
+        ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
+          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
+      (fun xz ab => S.place p
+        ((S.pointMeasExp p.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
+          (S.pointMeasExp p.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
+      S.psiHat ≤ C₂ * Real.sqrt ε)
+    (h₃ : ∀ p₁ p₂ : Placement, p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
+      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+        (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p₁
+          ((S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
+            (S.pointMeasExp p₁.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
+        (fun xz ab => S.place p₂
+          ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
+            (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
+        S.psiHat ≤ C₃ * ε)
+    (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂) :
+    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+        (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
+          S.place p₁ ((Q p₁.side xz).effect ab))
+        (fun xz ab => S.place p₂
+          ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
+            (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
+        S.psiHat ≤ 2 * η + 4 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 4 * (C₃ * ε) ∧
+      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+        (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
+          S.place p₁ ((Q p₁.side xz).effect ab))
+        (fun xz ab => S.place p₂
+          ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
+            (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
+        S.psiHat ≤ 4 * η + 8 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 8 * (C₃ * ε) +
+          2 * (C₂ * Real.sqrt ε) ∧
+      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+        (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) =>
+          S.place p₁ ((Q p₁.side xz).effect ab))
+        (fun xz ab => S.place p₂ ((Q p₂.side xz).effect ab))
+        S.psiHat ≤ 12 * η + 20 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) + 16 * (C₃ * ε) +
+          4 * (C₂ * Real.sqrt ε) := by
+  -- `R_1 ≈ M^X M^Z` on the opposite placement
+  have hRXZ := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+    _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ (h₁ p₁) (h₃ p₁ p₂ hopp)
+  -- `Q_1 ≈ M^X M^Z` on the opposite placement
+  have hQXZ := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+    _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ (hQR p₁) hRXZ
+  -- `Q_1 ≈ M^Z M^X` on the opposite placement

+    _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ hQXZ (h₂ p₂)
+  -- `M^Z M^X ≈ Q_2` on the opposite placement

+      (fun xz (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) => S.place p₂
+        ((S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
+          (S.pointMeasExp p₂.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
+      (fun xz ab => S.place p₂ ((Q p₂.side xz).effect ab))
+      S.psiHat ≤ 2 * η + 2 * (C₁ * Real.sqrt ε) := by
+    rw [opFamilyDistSq_symm]
+    exact opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+      _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ (hQR p₂) (h₁ p₂)
+  have hQQ := opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le (uniformDistribution (PointPair P))
+    _ _ _ S.psiHat _ _ hQZX hZXQ
+  refine ⟨by linarith, by linarith, by linarith⟩
+
+end ProjectiveSetting
+
+/-! ## Collapsing the error terms into one power -/
+
+/-- For `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`, the error terms `ε`, `√ε`, and `(C₀ (ε + √ε))^{1/4}`
+with `C₀ ≥ 1` are all bounded by multiples of `ε^{1/8}`. -/
+theorem error_terms_le_rpow_eighth {ε C₀ : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1)
+    (hC₀ : 1 ≤ C₀) :
+    ε ≤ Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) ∧ Real.sqrt ε ≤ Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) ∧
+      Real.rpow (C₀ * (ε + Real.sqrt ε)) (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤
+        2 * C₀ * Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) := by
+  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hε with h0 | hpos
+  · subst h0
+    have h8 : Real.rpow (0 : ℝ) (1 / 8 : ℝ) = 0 := Real.zero_rpow (by norm_num)
+    have h4 : Real.rpow (C₀ * (0 + Real.sqrt 0)) (1 / 4 : ℝ) = 0 := by
+      rw [Real.sqrt_zero, add_zero, mul_zero]
+      exact Real.zero_rpow (by norm_num)
+    rw [h8, h4, Real.sqrt_zero]
+    refine ⟨le_rfl, le_rfl, ?_⟩
+    positivity
+  · have hsqrt : Real.sqrt ε = Real.rpow ε (1 / 2 : ℝ) := Real.sqrt_eq_rpow ε
+    have hε1' : Real.rpow ε 1 = ε := Real.rpow_one ε
+    have hmono : ∀ y z : ℝ, z ≤ y → Real.rpow ε y ≤ Real.rpow ε z := fun y z hyz =>
+      Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge hpos hε1 hyz
+    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+    · exact le_of_eq_of_le hε1'.symm (hmono 1 (1 / 8) (by norm_num))
+    · rw [hsqrt]
+      exact hmono (1 / 2) (1 / 8) (by norm_num)
+    · have hsum : ε + Real.sqrt ε ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt ε := by
+        have : ε ≤ Real.sqrt ε := by
+          rw [hsqrt]
+          exact le_of_eq_of_le hε1'.symm (hmono 1 (1 / 2) (by norm_num))
+        linarith
+      have hC : 0 ≤ 2 * C₀ := by linarith
+      calc Real.rpow (C₀ * (ε + Real.sqrt ε)) (1 / 4 : ℝ)
+          ≤ Real.rpow (2 * C₀ * Real.sqrt ε) (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
+            apply Real.rpow_le_rpow (by positivity) _ (by norm_num)
+            nlinarith [Real.sqrt_nonneg ε]
+        _ = Real.rpow (2 * C₀) (1 / 4 : ℝ) * Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) := by
+            change (2 * C₀ * Real.sqrt ε) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) =
+              (2 * C₀) ^ (1 / 4 : ℝ) * ε ^ (1 / 8 : ℝ)
+            rw [Real.mul_rpow hC (Real.sqrt_nonneg ε), Real.sqrt_eq_rpow,
+              ← Real.rpow_mul hε]
+            norm_num
+        _ ≤ 2 * C₀ * Real.rpow ε (1 / 8 : ℝ) := by
+            refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (Real.rpow_nonneg hε _)
+            calc Real.rpow (2 * C₀) (1 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ Real.rpow (2 * C₀) 1 :=
+                  Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by linarith) (by norm_num)
+              _ = 2 * C₀ := Real.rpow_one _
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT
